title: ReaLM: Reliable and Efficient Large Language Model Inference with Statistical Algorithm-Based Fault Tolerance
problem: LLM accelerators face hardware faults from aging and variation; existing reliability methods require excessive voltage margins or expensive algorithm-based fault tolerance (ABFT) that ignore LLMs' inherent robustness.
motivation: Unreliable inference due to hardware faults compromises accuracy in safety-critical LLM applications; existing methods waste energy on redundant error recovery.
method: ReaLM co-designs circuit and algorithm with statistical ABFT that leverages LLM error tolerance; customizes error detection circuits for online error statistics collection and minimizes error recovery cost.
key_novelty: First systematic characterization of LLM inherent fault tolerance via large-scale error injection; statistical ABFT that adapts recovery based on learned error robustness.
contributions: Large-scale error injection study characterizing LLM fault tolerance
Statistical ABFT algorithm leveraging LLM error robustness
Low-cost error detection circuits (1.42% area, 1.79% power overhead)
Perplexity degradation reduced from 18.54 to 0.29, 35.83% energy efficiency improvement
primary_theme: statistical ABFT leveraging LLM inherent fault tolerance
